readout.purpose: Big figures in the stat row and the SLO verdict line (600). Mono, tabular.

title.purpose: The app name in the header only.

heading.purpose: Step panel titles, Summary of results, section headings; findings at 400.

body.purpose: UI text, button labels, rail labels; descriptions capped at 75ch.

data.purpose: Readouts at small size: table cells, chips, case names, status codes, legend values.

meta.purpose: Captions, notes under readouts and hints, in Barlow.

verdict.purpose: The findings headline sentence of a run, Barlow 600 at 28px.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Hover and press feedback on background, border, colour and transform.

motion.name: motion-base
motion.purpose: Progress fill (scaleX transform) and state changes.

motion.name: rise
motion.purpose: Results and views arriving; transform only, so content is never invisible.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce disables all animation and transition

components.description: The one main action at a decision point: Analyze, Generate cases, Start load test.

3 cases found bugs

    very_long_string_username ×11 · expected 4xx, got 200 {"username":"aaaaaaaa…"}
  • Server error (500) 2 cases: the server crashed on this input

narrative.overview:
Think of a bench instrument with a quiet graphite casing. The panels step back so the measured result comes forward. The casing is four close graphite layers with thin seams between them and no shadows. Everything that is a reading (a number, a URL, an ID, a payload, a status code) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. Everything that explains is set in Barlow. Colour appears only where a reading means something. Signal Teal marks what you can act on, and six status hues name how each request ended. Nothing is tinted for decoration.

The console is dense and calm. It is laid out for a laptop on a desk and for the same laptop on a projector during evaluation demos, so the verdict and the headline numbers must stay legible from the back of a room. It is dark only, with no light theme. Fonts are self-hosted (`code/frontend/public/fonts`), so the console renders offline exactly as it does online.

All colours, type sizes, spacing, radii, z-index values and durations live in `code/frontend/src/theme.js`. `applyTheme()` publishes them as CSS custom properties (`--c-*`, `--font-*`, `--type-*`, `--space-*`, `--radius-*`, `--z-*`, `--motion-*`). Components read colours from theme.js only.

**Revamped (November 2026).** The tokens, the colours, the meaning of each status colour and the type are unchanged from the original console. The ui-revamp replaced the single long page of numbered step panels with three views (New test, Run, History), moved mono to data only, and made every result lead with its findings. The sections below describe the revamped system.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite tonal layers (inset → page → panel → raised), separated by 1px seams. No shadows, no side tabs.
One action accent, Signal Teal, which never means "passed".
A fixed status palette whose meanings stay the same on every surface.
Mono for readouts, sans for words. Tabular figures everywhere.
Five type sizes. Hierarchy comes from weight and colour before size.
Findings first: bugs with their payloads, then coverage, then the SLO.
A 4px spacing scale. Gaps inside a group are smaller than gaps between groups.

rules.name: The Signal Is Not a Pass Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal marks what you can act on or where you are. Success is always Pass Green. A finished step's ✓ is teal because it is navigation state, not a test result.

rules.name: The Fixed Legend Rule
rules.body: A status colour means one outcome on every surface. Never reuse a status hue for decoration, branding or emphasis, and never pick a chart colour from the status set.

rules.name: The Name It Too Rule
rules.body: Colour is never the only carrier. Every outcome, verdict and state is also named in text (or `aria-label`), with a mark: ✓ ✗ ● ○ –.

rules.name: The Mono Means Measured Rule
rules.body: Mono is only for readouts: numbers, URLs, IDs, payloads, status codes and case names. It is never used for labels, headings, states or explanatory text. Table headers, field labels, step states and the health light are all Barlow.

rules.name: The Weight Before Size Rule
rules.body: Within one panel, set hierarchy with weight (600 vs 400) and colour (Readout White vs Caption Grey) before reaching for a new size. There are five sizes; don't add a sixth.

rules.name: The Back Row Rule
rules.body: Verdicts and headline numbers must be readable on a projector: Readout size, Readout White or their status colour, never Faint Grey. Faint Grey is only for things that don't matter from across the room.

rules.name: The Fold Rule
rules.body: The answer to "what happened?" is above the fold: Run opens at the top, and New test's Start stays visible while the cases scroll.

rules.name: The Clamp Rule
rules.body: Every single-column grid clamps its track (`grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr)`). A no-wrap payload or URL may cut with an ellipsis, but it never widens the page.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never cast shadows. To lift something, move it up one graphite layer. To draw attention to it, strengthen its seam.

dos: Do take every colour, size, space, radius, z-index and duration from `theme.js` / the `--c-*` custom properties. Components never hard-code hex values.
Do lead every result with its findings, then coverage, then the SLO.
Do use Signal Teal for actions, focus, progress, selection and the current view only, and Pass Green for passing.
Do pair every status colour with its name and an SVG icon, so no meaning depends on colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AA).
Do set data (numbers, URLs, IDs, payloads, status codes, case names) in IBM Plex Mono, and labels, headings, states and explanations in Barlow.
Do keep verdicts and headline numbers at 28px in Readout White or their status colour, so they read on a projector.
Do put an error directly under the control that caused it.
Do mark untested and "off" states with dashed outlines.
Do mark every approximate value with "≈" where it is read.

Do keep motion small: - a 6–8px rise when a view or a result arrives; - the progress fill; - pulsing run dots; - a short popover entrance. Animate only transform and colour (opacity only on popovers), and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't use mono for labels, headings or explanatory text.
Don't use Signal Teal to mean success, or Reject Amber (a 4xx colour) for general warnings. A warning is Readout White text with an alert icon.
Don't pick chart series colours from the status palette.
Don't add shadows, glows, gradients or thick coloured side borders.
Don't set anything a demo audience needs in Faint Grey.
Don't add a sixth type size or a second accent colour.
Don't explain things only in `title` tooltips; use a popover or a sentence.
Don't load fonts or assets from external hosts. The console must render offline.
Don't let a run with bugs or untested cases look all-green, or show an untested case as 0%.
